patent_grounding.rationale: Read the cited source text for the modeled chassis/wheel layout, nested linkset/platform, cylinder mounting options, steering linkage, guard mechanism, and guard drive. These passages support the claims made, including two actuator terminals coupling a chassis-to-linkset arrangement and steering-rod reciprocation represented internally in STEERING rather than as an external input.

functional_completeness.rationale: Revision 5 retains the principal patent-supported physical components and mechanisms, captures lift/steering/guard behavior, and removes the unsupported dangling boundary steering flow. No external hydraulic source or control details are guessed.

flow_consistency.rationale: The lift actuator now uses distinct mechanical linear terminals, each connected to one endpoint of the chassis-to-linkset mechanical coupling. No output branches to both endpoints; steering has a rotary flow to wheels, while internal rod/linkage reciprocation is behavior rather than a spurious unconnected boundary flow. Guard and platform flows have matching types and connected ports.

claim_traceability.rationale: Every cited model path is associated with relevant source passage IDs; the specifically changed actuator ports/interfaces and steering rotary ports/interface/flow carry citations. The citations substantiate the concepts rather than relying only on IDs.

interfaces.rationale: All listed interfaces reference extant subsystem and port IDs, have compatible mechanical flow types and direction, and are represented once at the owning subsystem. Distinct actuator ends model the supported mounting from chassis to linkset without the former shared-end branch. The steering rod has no dangling interface.

textbook_application.rationale: Guidance on distinguishing functions from physical subsystems and classifying interfaces is applied appropriately: components are physical subsystems, flows express mechanical interactions, and unspecified hydraulic source/control interfaces are omitted. Textbook guidance is not used as invention evidence.

summary: Independent review of SJS revision 5 focused on the actuator terminals, former dangling steering-rod flow, interface integrity, and the cited model content. The two mechanical actuator terminals are distinct and connected respectively to chassis and linkset, representing one of the patent's expressly supported arrangements without duplicate endpoint records or an implied branched terminal. Steering rod reciprocation remains an internal action of the steering subsystem; the boundary input and dangling flow are removed, while the supported rotary output to the steering wheels remains. Reviewed cited patent passages substantiate the model facts and changed elements. All six checklist categories pass; no unresolved issue identified.
